Advanced air sealing with drill-and-fill wall insulation was applicable to 92% of dwelling units. In theory, advanced air-sealing was applicable to 92.2% of baseline dwelling units, drill-and-fill wall insulation to 31% of baseline dwelling units, and about 30% of units could receive both measures as shown in Table 3. Below are results for only the applicable dwelling units. 4.2.1 Annual Stock Energy Analysis The average baseline applicable dwelling unit consumed 24.51 MWh of site energy per year. After air sealing and drill-and-fill wall insulation were applied to applicable units, the average dwelling unit consumed 19.20 MWh of site energy per year. This represents an average 21.7% decrease. Figure 3 shows the average energy consumption by end use per dwelling unit before and after the upgrade. Figure 3. Average energy consumption by end use group per applicable dwelling unit Before the upgrade, the largest two end uses in the average dwelling unit were natural gas heating and electric cooling. Other notable end uses included miscellaneous electric loads, electric appliances, and natural gas hot water heating. Significant savings are seen in heating and cooling end uses, particularly electric heating (35%), natural gas heating (40%), fuel oil heating (41%), propane heating (36%), electric cooling (11%), electric heating fan pumps (37%), and electric heat pump backup (54%). Slight savings are observed in the electric cooling fans and pumps (8%). End uses like water heating, lighting consumption, and miscellaneous electricity remain unchanged.
